I flew into this completely blind. I had heard of its existence some time ago, could not figure out how to get the stupid English patch I downloaded to work, and ended up shelving it before more-or-less forgetting about it completely.
Recently, however, it showed up for 75% off during the summer sale. This, combined with my now-twice piqued interest meant it was added to my cart instantly. I am not dissapointed.
I will preface this by stating that this isn't much of a game, so if you were expecting plenty of action and mashing of buttons, you are sorely mistaken. It's more of a semi-interactive novel, not all that far from a "choose your own adventure" book. You start off,  quite simply, as a teenaged human girl attending a school for birds (because what else would you expect?). The opening presents you with a run-down of the various relevant figures of your school. Every one of these has their own storyline that you can progress through by taking actions or making decisions favoring them. At the end, you get a unique ending specific to that character. You may also be presented with the "bad" ending if you somehow fail to endear yourself to any particular bird, though, with one exception, it's not really too hard to figure out what you need to do to charm your feathered fiancee.
And that's it. You now know how to "play" Hatoful Boyfriend.
That may seem like I'm cutting it a bit short, but I fear that getting any more in-depth about plot points is essentially impossible without spoiling one thing or another, especially in regards to a certain event that becomes available once you've received enough of the endings (yes, you do have to "date" Shuu). Very much of the game's appeal lies in the fact that it goes from exactly what the description implies (a silly, lighthearted title centered around dating pigeons), to a rather engrossing and intriguing story about how this odd world works. Moreover, there's little to say outside of "it's a thing where you read a lot of text and occasionally make a decision". That's not necessarily bad, but this isn't going to be something that appeals to you if you aren't the kind who enjoys an honest-to-god book every now and again.
Hatoful Boyfriend is not a purchase I regret, but it's not without its flaws. The most glaring is that much of the text is repeated, between storylines. There's a fast-forward button that will rapidly skip through text, however some scenes have the same beginning but diverge from there, meaning you might accidentally skip some dialogue you haven't read yet with this. A moderate familiarity with how the game goes helps prevent this, but that takes a few playthroughs and still isn't foolproof.
There are relatively few blemishes beyond that, and they're relatively minor, luckily enough. There are a few typos, although only one of them is major (you still get the gist of what's being said). There are some odd "between" frames of dialogue that are blank and require you to press the enter key, but there's no indication you need to do so other than that nothing is happening. The "level/stats" system is almost completely pointless, and I think is only really there for a few very specific scenes which probably could have got by without it anyway.
The redundant text is problematic, but it's not game breaking and the other downsides can mostly be overlooked. I question the price point of $10 full price, seeing as how there isn't any way to spend that much meaningful time on the game. I read fairly fast, and have essentially completed the game in well under 10 hours. Slower readers could reasonably expect somewhat longer than that. At sale price, especially as steep a sale as I got it on, it is well worth it.
I mean...come on you guys it's a pigeon dating sim. If that doesn't at least get you curious enough to skip out on your next bag of chips to shell out for it, you are sad, and I have no desire to associate with you any further than I already have. I bought LP3 some time ago during a Steam sale, and I was excited to finally get a chance to play it having loved the original two games. I understood that this entry to the series was going for a new feel with a more Westernized "Dead Space" feel. This too sounded exciting.
So now you can understand my large dissapointment when I attempted to load the game several times only to experience crashing issues every single time. After a series of driver updates, forum checking, and etc. I couldn't find a working solution to fix the game. So I assumed that perhaps there would be a patch eventually, thus I left it sitting on the back burner for several months now.
Here we are months later, and time to give this game another shot. It loads and runs! So I suppose that it was a problem on their end, but that all doesnt' matter now, its time to game! So apparently who ever was in charge of the keybinding section was a former ARMA developer, a keybinding for everything and each poorly placed. "Press P to pickup ammo". Seriously? I need to spam a key no the other side of the damn keyboard to get some ammo. Use the same damn key for my actions, E... like any other game with a competant keybinding. "But Damen, keybindings can be rebound! Stop complaining!" Sure they can, why should they need to be in the first place though? PC get the ♥♥♥♥ing 2nd hand treatment on this port too then? Didn't we learn from Borderlands?
Lets carry on. The sound in this game is ♥♥♥♥ing HORRIBLE. The voice acting is fine enough, but whoever did the levels really wanted you to know that the characters were talking. You can hear them over everything else in the world, disconecting you from it often. The monsters that you fight have roughly the same effect, almost making them annoyingly loud. Then there is the fact that you can still hear their shrill sounds and screaching while they are all dead and you're interacting with something.
Visually the game is passable. The map layouts and the structures are impressive enough, but the textures are very telling of this ports true target market, the consoles. I'm damn upset that Capcom wouldn't have shelled out a few extra bucks to get some higher resolution textures and some decent controls for the PC. Their money comes from our investments, and they need to step up their game. No pun intended.
Before I leave off, I want to touch one more time on the controls. When interacting with certain objects like using the mechs "rigs" claw to turn a giant X item, it pops up with "rotate claw using [w][a][s][d]" which would make you assume that you need to use all the keys. This isn't the case, and in fact I ended up rapidly smashing the d key several times over to very very very slowly rotate the claw. Attempting any other combination or series of key presses awarded me with no rotation. Other times the game wouldn't pop up with the rotation hint and wouldn't accept the key input at all. Go go gadget programer.
TL:DR ; ♥♥♥♥ this piece of poorly ported♥♥♥♥♥♥ Do NOT buy this game, no matter the price. Watch a damn "lets play" on youtube to learn the story if it matters that much.

A lot of nice ideas, but so poorly implemented… The game is officially no longer in alpha or beta, but don’t be fooled: it’s not and will never be finished. There is not even anything happening at the end of the game!
I ran into a tremendous amount of bugs. I couldn’t even play if the environment variable LC_ALL wasn’t set to C! A lot of people ran into this single critical issue since the early access, and it was never solved. It can be solved in 1 line of code, so it tells you how competent the developer is.
The “randomly generated open world” is a joke; nothing but a board with random tiles on it. Technically correct, but one would expect something like Minecraft or Don’t Starve. Even a Monopoly is more cleverly randomly generated than Pixel Piracy.
Also, it’s not really an open word as you’d expect : there’s a loading every minute.
It’s clearly a Rogue-like.
About the game in itself, it’s pretty boring. Once you spent an hour struggling with strange & buggy menus, you’ll understand an easy way to beat everything. For example, hire a fisherman and a cook is all you need to feed your crew for the rest of the game. You can also capture 4 hens to lay hundreds of eggs in order to heal your crew during battle. And you don’t need to build your ship; just capture others. Also, reload from the last checkpoint each time a crew member fails to mount on your ship.
That’s all, you will mainly have to wait during 5 hours (yes, most of the game consists in travels where nothing happens). And it’s the end. I guess. Nothing happens when you beat the game, as I said above.

I played Quake for the first time back in 1996, the year it came out. I rented it from a video/game rental place one day, and then I rented it a couple times more. I loved it. I thought it was the best thing ever.
I bought the boxed version on ebay a few years later, and then I bought it again on Steam. I've re-played it, start to finish, again this year, 20 years after its release - it was a spiritual thing. And while there have been many games after Quake that are really special to me, this one still has something that no other game since has had, and I can't really put my finger on it. It's something to do with the overall atmosphere of the game, monster and level design, Trent Reznor's haunting music... I don't know. If you like first person shooters and you've never played Quake, then just buy it and go play it immediately, you won't regret it.

Quake and Quakeworld is the game that holds dearest to my heart, of any game ever.
It's the game that got me into PC gaming, the community was small back then compared to today but the people who played it were passionate, obsessive and very competetive. But those people were a very tight family, a real community with a wonderful spirit  comradery. I've never come accross such a passionate group of people since and nor do I think I will in the future. Back then we had very little in terms of cutting edge hardware, we had 56k modems and Pentium II (if you were flash) with 32 MEGS! of RAM. You had to do the homework, write the scripts and binds, eek every last little bit out of your connection, the list goes on. Names like Sujoy, Clan 9 and Lakerman will only mean something to the few who were there at the time and I'd go back there in an instand just for one more game with those folks. But that day is gone in the name of progress, but the memories will last literally a lifetime.
And remember kids THIS is where rocket jumping started, FACT!
Quake is such an amazing game. It is fast paced, fun and gory. It has a good atmosphere and soundtrack. I would recomend this game to anyone who enjoys FPS or is trying to get into them.

If you wanna label RIFT, it's "Pay to Progress" and is entirely optional. Everything in-game can be bought and traded with in-game currency called "Platinum" It may take a bit of a grind, but everything you may want, you can get without ever spending a buck.
RIFT is your typical tab targeted MMORPG, but with a twist: You have 5 callings, Warrior, Mage, Cleric, Rogue and Primalist, These callings have each 9 souls you can play around with, creating your own playstyle, wanna be a tank with offheals? Done. Wanna be a melee Mage? Done. Each class has it's own resources, Mana, Energy, Power and Fury. And each class has it's own resource management ontop of class specific combo points.
It also has fun PvP events, An awesome playerhousing system, alot of zone puzzles, treasure cairns, fun places to explore,  a great RP community, and an awesome, although small-ish playerbase. We may be a small community, but everyone who joins feels welcome right away. There's also a bunch of us that offer information, free bags, a nice chat and silly jokes to keep the chats alive, and make newbies feel welcome.
Overall RIFT is a great game, but even great games have a downside: The latest expansion added an unfair and boring RNG element with Planar Fragments, you can compare this to Gems in other games, where it adds extra stats to boost your tanking/healing/dps. The fragments you get are tottaly random, and may or may not help you, depending on their stats and there's a chance you get the wrong stat once you upgrade it, making the entire fragment useless. Another problem the game has currently, is that the queue's for lowbie PvP and PvE take a good chunk of time. Mostly because newbies don't bother with healing/support/tanking souls, and when everyone plays as a dps, you won't get dungeons. On the other hand, there's a system called "Instant Adventures" or as we call them "IA's" Which are server wide raid events, across the entire world. It gives a good chunk of exp till level 60, but barely give anything else, leaving you vunerable once you start questing 60+.
TL;DR: Rift is an overall great game, with alot to offer. fun PvP events, A grand playerhousing, zone puzzles, treasure cairns and a great game for those who enjoy exploring. It's entirely "Free to Play" and doesn't cost you a dime. While the community is small, it's one of the greatest out there. It's free, so you got nothing to lose!
I rate this game a 8 out of 10. Amazing game with lots to offer.
Hope to see you in-game soon, and have fun exploring!

Psy High is a solid piece of interactive fiction.  Good, and worth full price, though not _great_.  I found it an enjoyable way to pass an hour and a half, and may replay it in future.
For those who haven't played a Choice Of game before, it's basically the natural evolution of Choose your Own Adventure Books, a few decades on.  They're MUCH more refined than the CYOA books of the 80s, though.  They're Wolfenstein: the New Order to the original Wolfenstein 3D.
You're given a short novel in which most important decisions are up to you, the reader.  Whether the plot twist you decide on succeeds depends on the choices you've made so far - staying in character is rewarded, while out of character actions are less likely to work.
The character in question is the sum of your past choices.  If at every turning point in the story so far, you've chosen to act like a selfish loner, don't expect to be able to successfully give an inspirational speech to rally others to your side.  I've you've chosen sports over academics whenever you've been able to, you'll almost certainly succeed at physical challenges (or those involving swaying the sports team or its fans) while not necessarily having a good chance of passing that crucial history test.
The story of Psy High is exactly as described.  If it were a live-action TV show, it wouldn't be (much) out of place on a DIsney afternoon line-up, or playing just before Charmed or Supernatural.
The writing is good enough to have often made me forget I was playing a game without graphics.  The characters are your usual high school stereotypes, but handled competently.  Choices have a satisfying level of consequence, but the game seldom presents you with unfixable mistakes.
In my playthrough, there were some strange jumps in the story near the end.  I can't tell if this was a deliberate editing choice, or if a few 'pages' were missing in error.  Though the jumps were a little jarring, I was still able to follow the story.  (Imagine an episode of 24 not accounting for fifteen minutes of the 24 hours, near the end.)
There were two pretty noticeable weaknesses to the story - first, the central plot was completely predictable from just a few minutes in.  A mystery to the reader, it certainly wasn't.
Second, although I think I chose the 'main' romance (kudos to Choice of Games for providing tons of tasteful choices for all preferences, as usual) it still felt pretty tacked on - almost as if most of the scenes and details had been added after the rest of the game was written.
Worth full price, but best for younger players (12-16).

Okay, so here is the deal.
Yes, the gameplay is altered substantially from the previous two, yes the T-Energy mechanic doesn't come into play sadly. I had hoped the game might have had a section as a nod to the old games where Jim's suit gets damaged but alas it did not.
Co-operative play is also not featured anywhere in the single player story.
This said however, while the gameplay is somewhere inbetween extreme condition and the first dead space title, the controls most of the time feel fairly fluid.
The characters, especially Jim Peyton himself are really likable and it kept me immersed in the story. Jim's wife is a very interesting character (as well as Jim himself)and the game has a lot of soul.
Jim isn't a grizzled space marine who can kill an akrid from 300 metres, but he is also not out of his depth.
With a temperament somewhere between a trucker and a cowboy he instantly became (for me) one of my favourite videogame protagonists of all time
When you're out there on your own, with just music you brought from planet earth (the game imports music from your computer files so you can creat your own soundtrack for the cold wastelands) you really feel like there's no-one else you can count on but yourself. You feel isolated and in danger at every second.
This also works in reverse, that when you get a message from your in game wife you feel like you're at home, like you're making a difference and the characters really come to life. The same can be said when you return to coronis and upgrade your rig and weapons, greeting old friends.
There's a fair bit of longevity in the upgrades to your rig. Certain upgrades allow you to get to new places you couldn't before, or allow you to scrounge for scrap metal in new places.
The controls when fighting the akrid will feel a little alien at first due to the over the shoulder viewpoint of the camera, but you quickly get used to the contextual-only use of the grappling hook as well as dodging out of the way of enemies.
Fans of the series will be pleased to know that this does actually provide an interesting and very unexplained part of the story of the franchise and while they do retcon one or two things, it really does feel like it's for the better. The plot makes sense and while isn't anything spectacular, it is coherent and well-written. The supporting cast for me, was what really pulled along the plot for me and kept me interested even while trying to hunt down those annoying albino akrid.
The setpieces out in the ice and snow are quite fantastic and this is where the game excels, in the sheer scale of the areas outside. The opposite is unfortunately true in that on the occasional offchances you go into an enclosed space, combat and movement can feel clunky and out of place.
It's a shame likely the repetitive sidequests will put anyone off buying this because the atmosphere is amazing.
You really do feel like a lone contractor out in the middle of nowhere drilling for a precious substance.
I imagine the feeling and atmosphere in this game is not all that disimilar from the feelings of isolation and longing that ice truckers deal with on a day to day bonus.
Which brings us to the Rigs. The rig is not the vital suit (this is a prequel don't forget), it is an entirely different breed of machine, but this isn't a bad thing.
Yes, there are a few mechs in this game and while at first you may lament the loss of having shoulder mounted rockets and gatling guns, you will immediately warm up to the defensive and offensive capabilities of Jim's machine. Admittedly the rig can feel quite slow at times and while this may have been an artistic choice by the devs at Spark it can bog down the pace at times until you access fast travel quite early in the game. The good news is that those who loved the sheer mayhem and carnage of slicing off a limb or two from the large akrid will be right at home. It is just as satisying, maybe moreso to time your grab just right as you hold the creature and helplessly drill into it's cores with the drill arm as their lifeblood (T-energy) spills out.
I should point out that I was only ever interested in the game (and series) for the single player experience and therefore I did not touch multiplayer. My understanding is some of the maps from extreme condition make a reappearance and generally most reviewers say the online is where the strength of the game really lies.
This game did poorly due to the mountain of scathing critiques and generally poor write-ups it received.
I personally enjoyed it and would recommend it to anyone who was a fan of the series for the story.
In terms of all the bad press and poor scores, I'd advise you to try it for yourself, it's not the most amazing game in terms of graphics or presentation but I sure had fun with it.

This game.  What more is there to say about this game beyond what has been said already?  It purports to be a bird dating sim, but under the zany surface, it is so much more.  There are multiple routes through the story, each matching you with a different avian.  Every route is some combination of hilarious, sad, and disturbing.  The writing is entertaining, and the game is very self-aware.  You'll think you're laughing at the game, and then you'll realize you've been laughing with it the entire game.
But after you get your laughs (and maybe a few tears) from the dating routes, a new option will open up.  The "Bad Boys Love" route is the true heart of this game.  It is a well-written, fascinating, suspenseful tale that ditches the veneer of "wacky bird dating sim" completely.  All of the little details from each of the dating routes come together in unexpected ways.  I hesitate to say more, for fear of spoiling it, but rest assured, it's worth it.  You'll laugh, you'll cry, you'll encounter unexpected nightmare fuel, and you'll definitely never look at pigeons the same way again.
So, really, to enjoy this game, you need to be a certain kind of person.  If you appreciate good writing, hold humor and serious (even disturbing) content in equally high esteem, and can get over the fact that all the characters are birds, give this game a go.  You might just fall in love.

I give Pixel Piracy a thumbs down, but with 2 caveats; if you can get it for less than $5, or if the developers end up releasing some major patches then it might deserve a thumbs up. Also, as of this writing, I only have ~8 hours in and have not seen all of the game elements, so if my opinion changes later I will update this review... Feel free to downvote my review, but if you do please leave a comment as to why you didn't find it helpful. I'm trying to provide an honest and meaningful review, so if there are issues with it I'd really like to know!
Pixel Piracy has its moments, but they are nearly always overshadowed by poor design choices. The clunky UI, lack of variety, and various issues relegate Pixel Piracy to the bargain bin. There is fun to be had and there is certainly some charm, but not enough to overcome some glaring issues that should’ve been corrected before the game was fully released. 5/10.

The interface is pretty terrible, and there is almost no explanation of how to play, the only information on how to play the game is found in a text menu, and even that is missing quite a bit of information. I found myself constantly using online guides until I figured things out for myself, but then I was missing stuff I didn’t even know I needed to know.

In roughly 7 hours, it looks like I’ve barely scratched the surface of the map I started on. However, the map is limited by the lack of different events in the game: ship battles, island battles, and towns (I don’t count sailing since it requires no input from the player and is only there to show transition of time). Each has some slight variations (e.g., different shop types in different towns, an island full of pandas, etc.), but the variations are very minor and don’t add enough to keep the experience from getting stale quickly. The best illustration I can think of for this is islands, Almost every island you land on will have the same layout: some sort of bush (healing, hurting, or both), an interactive item (totem, pile of bones, etc.), and then a chest(s) in that order.

It’s very simple, and there is almost no variety in the building blocks, but it’s still good fun to build a pirate ship!

Level up; learn jobs; learn combat techniques; equip a passive item, melee and ranged weapons. While leveling up and training your pirates is fun, there are some major issues. There are various jobs you pirates can learn (e.g., cooking, cleaning, fishing, etc.). The biggest issue is that some of these jobs are mutually exclusive (e.g., your fisherman cannot also be your cannoneer), yet the game never tell you that, and will allow you to waste money and resources teaching a pirate both jobs. Also the inventory is atrocious as you can only see it by trying to equip a pirate with an item and then it will show everything in that category in the order you picked it up, it’s cluttered and ugly.

Pirates and Creatures erupt into fountains of pixelated blood and body parts making battles visually entertaining. However, controlling battles is clunky and annoying. Clicking the left mouse button over an enemy will tell your captain to attack that enemy (don’t be surprised if your captain forgets your order and starts attacking someone else). As for your crew, if you don’t tell them specifically what to attack by pausing, then clicking and dragging them to a specific target, they will either attack whatever the captain is attacking or whatever they come into contact with first, and even if you do tell them who/what to target specifically they will likely forget and start attacking someone else. While you can group your pirates into various categories they can’t be in more than one, so issuing orders becomes tedious micromanagement, or you throw it all out the window and just let them do their thing and hope for the best.

You can’t be a legitimate pirate without a parrot on your shoulder, and Pixel Piracy lets you do that (theoretically at least). I love the idea of pets, but capturing them is an absolute mess. To capture an animal you have to equip an Animal Cage in a pirates ranged weapon slot. If it’s anyone but your captain you’ll have to pause and then click and drag them to target the animal. With either your captain or a crew member you’ll have to constantly issue the order as they’ll only throw the cage 1-2 times before giving up or attacking the animal (there’s a 5% chance to caputre, so get ready to issue the order frequently). On top of that you have to ensure that the animal doesn’t get within melee range of your pirate or your pirate will switch to their melee weapon and attack the animal.
There is no story to speak of. It’s not a terrible thing especially considering that Pixel Piracy is a rouge-like, but some story elements might’ve helped make the game world feel more alive.
The currently popularity of retro graphics (and the “Pixel” in the title) makes the graphics acceptable; however, the developers have done nothing to make their graphical choice any more impressive. Every island pretty much looks the same, there are only a handful of different building blocks for the ships, the pirates all look the same, etc. In short there’s nothing to get excited about, but it works for the style of game. The sound on the other hand is outright atrocious, there are a few different voices but they’ll constantly call out the same phrase (hopefully you like hearing, “Avast ye’ scallywags!” if not, you might want to turn the volume down.), chickens cluck at least every 10 seconds, so if you’re on an island/ship expect to hear that way more than you care to. It seems like the developers even recognized that the sound design was bland as the game came with Music and SFX turned off by default. I tried playing with them on, but quickly got tired of them.
I really want to love Pixel Piracy, and I see a lot of potential in it, but its bevy of issues keep me from truly liking it. I give it 5/10. There is enough fun to justify one play through but it’s not something I’d replay. Supposedly the developers are still working on the game, if that is the case and there are some major fixes this game could become seriously good.

I have an annotated Comments/Concerns list. I'm very early in my time on this game so take it for what that's worth. This will be updated after I put more hours into the game.
Comments
-Simple: too many games want to do a crazy deep web of interactions that to be honest, most of the time I don't fully explore or don't find some paths appealing. This game gives you a straightforward premise and off you go.
-Depth: Right now I am trying to figure out the best way to set up towers so that if they are destoryed my units can fall back most effienctly. I have not played a game where I had developed micro stratagies since perhaps Stronghold Crusader when I was young. Usually I just find the op stratagy and spam it ( or more frustratingly the game tells you what the op strat is ). This game is making me think and strategize which is personal plus.
-Time commitment: So far I love the flexability of a playing session. I find with most singleplayer games to do whatever it is I want to do will take hours. While this is good because you get time out of the game, I don't always have hours and hours to do a string of quests or explore new maps. This is a game that you can pour half a day into or do just an hour at a time.
Concerns
Difficulty: Games like this can be easily demolished by becoming too difficult or too easy (see Darkest Dungeon for reference). As the developers add units,building maps etc I could see it tipping the wrong way in a hurry. Not to say I don't expect growing pains ( buffing and nerfing new content ) but I hope they don't make a fundamental change that will put this game in a different difficulty range.
Overall this game is really fun. Its simple but challenging which is the recipe for a great game. As it stands right now I highly recommend this game to anyone. Provided it doesn't fall off a cliff with fundamental changes I see this being a really strong title.

**Please don't hesitate to leave a reply here with any questions or otherwise you might have. If you disagree, feel free to leave a comment as well. I have tried my best to remain as objective as possible.**
Where to start... I have played RIFT since 2013, and I have logged thousands of hours on this game (I only used the Steam client to launch it a few times, hence my low hours played here). I went from playing alone to being a part of one of several hardcore progression raiding guilds, spending hours in-game, grinding, having fun and downing next to impossible raid bosses with my friends and guild members. I created and maintained an entire website for raid guides and more for this game, which is still up today at
, even though it's of no matter now. I used to play with the devs, testing new raid mechanics as well as other new features they wanted to implement. I loved this game. Then, Starfall Prophecy (Prophecy of Ahnket) happened. This expansion cost $60 or $40 to pre-order. What was left of the raid scene was ecstatic for its release, as it was going to give us a new raid, a new raid tool, and more. Then... It released. I don't want to type too much, so I'll just give a list of why this expansion does nearly everything it can to kill its playerbase.
- In this expansion, they did away with gear having secondary stats on them (attack power, spell power, etc.), and replaced them with a slot on each piece of gear that needed to be filled. I.e. You get a gear drop, and you don't have a secondary stat. You need to find a fragment with that stat to fill the slot. Here's the issue: You can buy fragments. You can buy boxes with fragments in them. This is a money grab any way you look at it. This system wasn't necessary, and we didn't ask for it. Each fragment has several 'levels' that have to be upgraded. This costs a MASSIVE amount of in-game currency, which can be indirectly bought by buying REX (which grants in-game buy only currency) and selling them to other players for platinum (This has been a thing for a while, but platinum, the in-game currency, had never been viable for purchasing or upgrading gear... until now). This is pay-to-win by any definition if your definition includes selling gear. I'm not one to scream pay-to-win all that often, but I think by most people's definition, this is, especially since fragments can drop that are not even for the class you play. They are lazily bundled into one massive loot table.
- The class balance in PvP and even PvE 'content' (Which is lacking, and I'll touch on later), is disgusting. In PvP, there are still broken abilities that can one shot other players, and abilities that can make players invincible. The management has explicitly stated that 'they don't focus on PvP', which begs the question: 'why have it at all if you aren't going to make it better?'. Rift's selling point was always the soul system, which allows every class (Mage, cleric, etc.) to play every role (healing, tanking, etc.). However, in PvE, the balance is so awful, that the vast amounts of the souls you can use are utterly useless compared to others. The class developer will not take constructive criticism nor acknowledge these problems, instead saying 'he knows best', and proceeding to ignore any and all player feedback (read the forums and it will prove this point, thread after thread of feedback completely ignored).
- Before the release of Starfall Prophecy (Prophecy of Ahnket), we were promised a new raid. This sounds lacking, but Rift's development team is so small already, it's all we could hope for.  Before the release of the expansion, they got rid of their raid developer. They continued to promise the new raid even after the release of the expansion, and they finally announce it for March in the 4.1 update (Prophecy of Ahnket is 4.0)... except we didn't get a raid. We received a 10 man entry level expert that could be cleared over and over again using 'individual reward charges' to randomly receive gear. (These charges can be bought in the store...). PvP was completely ignored (There is no dedicated PvP developer). They then promised a new raid... Which is a rehash (copy) of a previous raid from the original RIFT release, along with releasing a new 'expert dungeon'... again, a rehash from the previous nightmare tide expansion.
- An example: Several days ago, a forum post was created regarding the loot crates that you buy on the store (which give you completely useless items unless you get the one thing in the box you have a 0.5% chance of winning; seriously, the real chance is approximately that). The community manager posted, saying they never received any feedback from players regarding how to make the boxes better. Players responded, linking several long and well thought-out posts about how to improve the boxes and make them worth the $5 they cost. The community manager responds, saying that "linking posts sarcastically is not helping anyone", completely ignoring the linked posts and the copy/paste feedback. The test server feedback threads are completely ignored by class and content devs, suggestions are ignored unless they were already being implemented, in which a producer or the CM will respond with "We will do this", pretending that the feedback was actually considered, even though it was being implemented already.
- I had an entire section here outlining how I felt that Starfall Prophecy was unfairly and indirectly charging money for gear, even though it wasn't directly for sale. Now, it seems that has changed. As of December, Trion is officially selling boxes of the current tier currency for real money/credits only, disregarding any argument that was left defending Rift from being pay-to-win. You can now buy the best-in-slot gear for real world money with no setbacks.
Is there ANYTHING good you have to say? - For the prophecy of Anket? No. However, Rift's lifeline, the player housing system, is still shining brightly. This is the only developer who I have seen interacting on the forums with the players. New dimension assets are being released frequently. Tacitus, thank you for setting an example for your fellow co-workers. If only they'd follow your footsteps.
- Poor optimization (More than 10 players in one area can cause very low frame rates for no apparent reason, ranging from 10-20 FPS at best, and it's not a system issue, it's on their end), server crashes (the servers crash on a fairly regular basis, especially after an update), Bugs galore (broken bosses in raids and dungeons, broken abilities, exploitable bugs that will get you banned for simply mentioning them (This has happened before; a group of players were banned in-game for reporting an exploit)), lack of content in most areas (questing and player housing/dimensions are all that's left in terms of content), and more, too much to type. This is not the game it appears to be.
Rift is not the game is used to be. If you want fun and engaging/challenging PvP or PvE content, this is not the game for you. The Community manager has openly stated several times if you want this type of gameplay, 'Rift is not for you', calling people who have left feedback or suggestions on the forums 'sarcastic' (This is fact, not me being angry). It's sad to see what has happened to this game I used to care so much for, but times change. If you have any questions or feedback for this review, PLEASE don't hesitate to leave a comment, and I'll happily answer objectively as I can. If you disagree, by all means, tell me, and maybe you can change my mind. I am not 'salty', and I do not hold a grudge against the company, but I do think that people need to read these types of reviews before deciding to sink time or money into games like this and others.  I will update my review if they do make any positive changes.

enjoy this chicken stir fry recpie
- Serves 4
- 10 mins to prepare and 10 mins to cook
- 325 calories / serving
- Healthy
INGREDIENTS:
- 1 orange, zested and juiced
- 2tbsp soy sauce
- 2tbsp sesame oil
- 250g (8oz) tender stem broccoli
- 5cm (2in) piece root ginger
- 1tbsp sunflower oil
- 1 garlic clove, finely sliced
- 1 red pepper, deseeded and thinly sliced
- 150g Straight To Wok Noodles
- 400g (13oz) chicken fillet, cut into thin slices
METHOD
Step 1 - Mix together the orange zest and juice, soy sauce and sesame oil and set aside.
Step 2 - Blanch the broccoli in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain well and set aside.
Step 3 - Finely shred the ginger. Then heat a large frying pan or wok, add the sunflower oil, heat it until sizzling, and fry the ginger till it's crisp.
Step 4 - When it's done, remove with a slotted spoon. Add the chicken and garlic, and stir-fry until just browned. Remove the meat using a slotted spoon and set aside.
Step 5 - Add the red pepper and broccoli and stir-fry for around 2-3 minutes until it's just tender. Add the soy sauce mixture, bring it to the boil then return the chicken to the pan

3rd person, squad based, action, tactical shooter versus aliens. This game is about Alien invasion on a late 1900's Earth. You play as a XCOM Agent, carefully selected people who were professionals in their field of work, before joining the The Bureau. Be it in CIA, FBI, NSA and other agencies.
XCOM is a secret US government facility, made to counter invasion attempts on US soil. Game has really good story but a bit not realistic with all the "borrowing alien technology" aspect. World art style is mix of 1950-1970's retro and futuristic alien sci-fi elements.
There are many weapons in the game, from WWII pistols, rifles, shotguns, sniper rifles, grenades to sci-fi alien weapons, that share similar concepts (plasma pistols, plasma rifles, shotguns, sniper rifles, etc.). All alien weapons are energy based, with their own ammunition.
You can recruit different types of soldier classes, that are experts in their field of combat. Be it simple engineer, that can deploy turrets, sniper that can deal heavy damage from range, commando who can absorb damage and taunt enemies, or support class that can boost your squads damage, increase survivability, etc.
Each class has their own skill tree, abilities and weapon preferences. One is good at range, other can survive a lot of punishment, third can manipulate the battlefield to your advantage, etc.. Personal and squad abilities can be chained from tactical "Focus" mode, you can very easily position your soldiers, order them to focus one target, revive injured ally.
AI is very good and will often flank you, flush you out of cover and rush up on you, depending on what alien unit it is. Game environment and level design is great, with a lot of room for flanking and surprise attacks. Enemy variation is also good, with close range, long range units mixed with air and stealth units.
Game is somewhat similar to XCOM: Enemy Unknown in some aspects. You control, improve, gear up your squad, send them on rescue, Intel missions or accompany them on more harder side missions apart from main story missions. You can recruit only male soldiers for your squad, if someone wanted females, it's not possible. Sadly you don't research alien technology yourself, or make items, those are automatically managed by game and XCOM Agency itself.
Game has a lot of character dialogues, with choice and effect, consequence system. Voice acting is good, texture quality and visuals are good, character control and animations were decent. Game is about 15 hours long and was a blast to playthrough. It's not as punishing as XCOM: Enemy Unknown, being a shooter, game is fairly forgiving and there's a lot of room for personal error, compared to XCOM: Enemy Unknown.
Game was very fun and enjoyable.

I recommend this game with a caveat. Read on. But first off: This is NOT an XCOM game. If you want XCOM, look elsewhere.
This game looks pretty good, runs like absolute balls. Disable PhysX whatever you do. I went from 12 FPS in PhysX areas to 120+. It is NOT optimized for PhysX in any way.
I played through the game on Veteran skill and I feel the challenge was overall fair. The combat is very reminiscent of the Mass Effect series, but I'd argue that it's actually better. The actual combat is pretty fun, although some enemies can feel overly bullet-spongy at times. Particularly the "miniboss" characters such as Mutons and Sectopods. This is compounded by the fact that you are forced to relocate around the battlefield constantly, as all the weapons have very limited ammo stocks, so you have to scrounge for ammo refills around the area. Keep in mind though that this is in no way a strategy game like its predecessor. This is a 3rd person squad-based cover shooter with tactical elements.
The combat has plenty of variety in areas, enemy setups and equipment for your squad. Squad-classes are well diverse and you actually feel like you sometimes need a particular class in a particular battle to succeed, in difference from Mass Effect where you can go with basically anyone and still kick♥♥♥♥♥
I found myself dying a couple of times throughout the game and had to replay a few battles with better tactics, so I'd say difficulty and combat mechanics are spot on (aside the bullet-sponginess).
The story is dumb. It's super dumb. I found myself cringing heavily during cutscenes when the characters were speaking. It really feels like no one in this game has half a brain to think with and they're regurlarly acting downright stupid and illogical at most times. Don't get me wrong though: The lore and the alien world/design is pretty cool and interesting. It's just the humans that are absolute toshpots. Especially the main character, Carter, seems like an absolute gorilla who thinks with his hormones.
The game has issues with pacing. Sometimes it's easy to follow along the story missions and have a good pacing going, but then suddenly everything grinds to a halt and you have to faff about the base for 30 minutes (I hate all the running around) and then suddenly there are no story missions. Just side missions. So you HAVE to faff about pointless side missions. Not sure I'm a fan of that.
In conclusion:
Is this game any good? Yeah, I'd say it is. It has its problems absolutely, but I had overall fun. My absolute biggest gripe is the story and writing and how the main characters react to things. I won't spoil anything but some decisions in this game really made me want to eat my desk and the ending is absolute♥♥♥♥♥ Such a cop out story ending I nearly laughed.
But I still recommend it as it was, for the most part, very enjoyable.

In my eyes, a real underrated jewel of objective-based shooters.
It has a system that allows one to create your own weapon, much like Blacklight: Retribution allows you to do. The point is, new players don't know what to put on their weapon and will end up with a "bad" weapon. This may be something to put you off.
The whole SMART thing that was going on: it's bound to Shift and it's basicly the same as sprint, but it does allow you to climb walls and stuff, wich is kinda neat, but if you really want to use it, you'll have to play as a light, low health character, witch come with their own problems.
Weapon parts are unlock trough, what essentially is, a training mode. Unlike other games, like CoD, this allows you to unlock all weapons and attachments, as long as you're good enough to get them.
The whole problem are the perks. Much like CoD, you get perks wich benefit you in one way or the other, you get to choose one perk per level, much like you would in an RPG. Levels are divided by "level brackets", to make sure a new level 1 player wouldn't have to face off against a level 30 character. This promised a plain playing field, as everyone has access to about the same stuff, if they so desired. In the current state this poses another problem; there are barely enough people playing to fill one server, let alone one for each level bracket. Fortunately, the level brackets can be turned off, but as you guessed, this does impact the game.
The AI is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. Even on the highest difficulty, they barely pose any thread at all. Half the time you lose it's because you AI teammates weren't there you help you, to keep you alive as you attempt to complete an objective.
So all in all: it works as co-op shooty bro-bro fun time, and it would work as a competitive shooter would more people play this.

I love this game. I do. I'm not gonna lie and say it doesn't have its faults. It has plenty. The storyline is cornier than a Bold and Beautiful Marathon, the races are either rage-quit hard or stupid easy (mostly the former), and the physics make a good portion of the cars feel like intoxicated Wookies. However, it is still amazingly fun. The environments, while not in the most amazing graphics out there, are beautiful and engaging. The roads and curves are better than even Forza Horizon 2. The money rewards from events are slightly low, as well.
All of this said, I have fixed plenty of these problems with some tinkering. With an unpacked game, the car list can be almost doubled, plenty of other mods can be added with a few tools, and things that you wouldn't normally have access to can be accessed. I would of course get the game on sale. An unpacked game can allow most of the soundtrack to be changed, because I know that there are weak points in the music selection, and many of them. I have had great fun with this game for years, and I think you can, too. With a little more love than it got, it can be loads of fun. With a little research, an abundance of tools can be found to enhance this game, and as someone who isn't that experienced, I learned a lot about modding through it. It's not that hard once you start doing it.

Prison Run and Gun:
~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
Living in a small room (1.8 X 2.4 meters) for most of your days is rather confronting, especially if you’re claustrophobic. Well, this has been your life for quite a while since you were sentenced and sent to prison. There are more downsides than upsides in this type of establishment, but today is different. A prisoner has created chaos in the joint and this might be your opportunity to finally escape this hell hole. Make your run for freedom in Prison Run and Gun!

Prison Run and Gun is an action / platformer game where you take control of an inmate and try to escape a prison facility throughout 30 levels.
What do you need to successfully escape a prison? Well, you probably need a detailed plan of the building, which you don’t have. All you know is that you have to reach the other side of each room you enter to get closer to freedom.
At the start of each level, your character will only carry the conventional orange prison suit. The puzzles are quite simple and consist of destroying crates, explosive barrels and activating switches within a stage to be able to reach the next room. There are other obstacles, such as mines, flying objects carrying mines, still machine guns, electric barriers, fire, round saws, men on flying missiles and waiters who are carrying mines for your main meal. The good news is that you will be able to destroy most of these objects, with the exception of the saws.
Look for cases, as they have items such as guns, grenades and helmets which you’ll need to successfully clear a stage. Bear in mind that grenades come in short supply. There is also a case which holds a key within each level and they are usually the hardest to reach.
The gameplay is fun and simple; your character jumps around, destroys obstacles with guns or his helmet and if you die, you restart the level until you succeed. It’s not a really difficult game but it’s very addictive.  I really like the pixel artwork and I enjoy the funky music but it would have been nice to have more tracks. The controls work perfectly whether you use a gamepad or the keyboard, which is great. Another good point - this game is well priced for its content. Marvellous!
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Great pixel artwork
-	30 levels to beat
-	Well-designed levels
-	Fun and addictive gameplay
-	Good price point
-	Achievement and trading cards
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	Needs to be slightly harder
-	Needs more tracks (music)

Gee, where do I begin? Land Ho! Land Ho! Land Ho! Land Ho! That's a percent of what you'll hear in this game. That's it. Somebody at the developer forgot that games need music. I was reminded of three things in my hour-ish stint of many restarts in this game: Dwarf Fortress, Early Access, and lack of content.
Dwarf Fortress is an incredible game. It'll never be fully optimized or sold out but it'll always get content updates and as of right now it's actually playable for a good extent before the sheer bulk of everything destroys your computer's CPU. That's a discussion for another time. Reading the crew descriptions was pretty cool and I know that's what they were inspired by. I'm glad they took inspiration from Dwarf Fortress but Dwarf Fortress can do without music because it's a F2P game run by donations. It does, however, have a catchy intro tune that does work and a simple, yet pleasing, tune.
Instead, all I heard was annoying pixels shout pirate cliches over and over. I know I'm a pirate in the pirate world. I can read all the Pirates of the Caribbean references and know that those were basically obligatory. I don't need the frequency of it to be so often. Of course, someone had the bright idea to add a voice option slider. Which was actually a good idea. It doesn't cover up the fact that there's no music, of course, but it's something.
Early Access. I bought this on the recent Steam sale on a whim. Because why not? It was like three dollars. I had never heard of it before and I am not surprised. Seemed like an interesting premise. I'm glad I bought it for the low price I did, because paying for the privilege of watching me "sail" to my next destnation (you're on your raft, 'sailing', which is really just a percentage in the upper right corner of the screen) is not what I expected. Bravo. Thanks for the privilege. You'll soon be surprised to find out that there's no fast forward button at all. Low on health? Better go read a book, because it'll take it's sweet time regenerating independent of where you are. Chest on the other side of the island? Stroll over there and pick it up of course! What? That's it? Two or three animals on an 'island', one object to interact with, and a chest containing 7 gold? What do you mean that's an island?
The lack of content in this is so glaring I'm kind of shocked. Music is nonexistent, so there's no immersion or atmosphee (truth be told I would have to disable voices to even get that immersion should music be patched in). Islands feel empty. I guess islands also only have one coconut tree that drop a singular coconut? Uh thanks? I just lost 20 hp and that's what I get? 4 gold? What? What do you mean the crab hit me for 8 health?
To top it all off is the toilet humor of your pirates literally defecating on your ship. Unless there's an unseen timer for defecating it's completely random. Oh. The best part? You have to spend 30 gold (you start with 50) to teach one pirate how to use the bathroom properly AND spend a skill point. Not that your ship has one, obviously. It's just a raft. It's mind-boggling to think that this is how pirates used the bathroom on ships in the last centuries- by taking a dump right on the ship. Incredible. I'm not a maritime expert of the 16th century or what-have-you, but I would think at the very least pirates and sailors took their dumps in a locale that went out of the ship or in a confined space. I can't believe I'm even talking about this in a review.
I'm just glad the developers didn't go all the way (one of your starting bonus options is a second crew member, you being the first, with the title of the Flatulent) and make slip hazards out of it. Unsurprisingly, having a large amount of fecal matter on your ship decreases morale of your crew. Go figure.

Most of the people who buy this game just play it for the LOLs and to be able to brag about playing a dating simulator with birds (it's a great conversation starter, alright). oh my god.
i bought hatoful boyfriend less than 48 hours ago, and after getting all of the achievements, i don't even know where to begin.
i'll avoid spoilers as best as i can, but if you're really wanting to avoid any and absolutely ALL spoilers, you should probably stop reading this review about here.
originally i bought this game as something of a joke, since i'd heard good things about it, and it was on sale.  of course, my initial reaction was "lol bird dating sim", but as i played more of it, i started to get a creeping feeling that things weren't exactly as happy as they seemed.
cue google, finding the hatoful boyfriend wikipedia, and finding out that my hunter-gatherer instincts were spot-on, though i did my best to avoid anything too spoiler-filled.
so i decided to take my time, and play through all of the routes, since this is how you unlock the route that gives, basically, the entire backstory of the world, even explaining the existence of sentient birds.
(**mild/vague spoilers beyond here.**)
none of the initial dating routes are too overly long, but they're very enjoyable.  for your reference, these are the dating routes you can go-
- ryouta (childhood friend, bittersweet ending)
- sakuya (bird nobility who's kind of a jerk, two slightly different endings [neither soul-crushing])
- okosan (PUDDING is literally the only thing to say about this bird; if you've just gone a soul-crushing route, do this one next [two different endings with him too])
- kazuaki (the cute teacher, slightly sad but sweet ending)
- nageki (shy + depressed introverted kid, absolutely SOUL-SHATTERING ENDING.  I LITERALLY CRIED.)
- yuuya (kinda a playboy, relatively happy ending)
- shuu (the creepy doctor, don't even ask about his endings.  don't do it.  [also two different endings.])
- azami (??? adding her to this list because it's kind of a route, though i don't know that it 100% counts?  w/e, she's cute and her ending is really cute too.  two different endings as well, though only one is with the mc.)
really though, there's so much more to the characters than what i've mentioned- i've only just barely touched the tip of the iceberg, quite honestly.
after finishing the all of the routes, you'll be prompted with an option after the initial settings.  the first option lets you have a normal game, while the second brings you to an alternate route that, as i mentioned, gives the backstory of the world, and a lot of the characters.  technically you don't need every single route completed to unlock it the route itself, but i'd recommend it in order to get the epilogue, which is unlocked by getting the rest of the endings in the game.
god, though.  i don't think i can recommend this game highly enough?  i legitimately thought it would be exclusively happy fun times, but haha, no.  i can't even tell you how many times i ended up crying over these dumb birds, wondering at myself how my life came to this point.
play hatoful boyfriend.
you won't regret it.
(or if you do, it'll only be due to the fact that this bunch of dumbass birds ruined your life, like they did mine.)

If there's one thing I can't stand, it's nostalgia. A culmination of memories and experiences that often lead to the misinterpretation of what you are experiencing. I have read through a good number of reviews for this game, and the big commonality is nostalgia. Players claiming that they played way-back-when and how great the game was at some time or another. People complaining that the decisions of the company are only to hurt their community and the players within. Throughout all the negativity over this Free To Play MMOROPG, I will give my opinion of the game. Hopefully this will give some insight into the game that isn’t just “This game is worse than it used to be,” or “My captcha wouldn't work so heres a negative review.”

The short version:
Rift is a good game. If you enjoyed playing World of Warcraft during the base game or its first expansion, The Burning Crusade, then you will likely enjoy this game. It is something you can play fully from the Free To Play model, or enjoy the cosmetic and time saving rewards that come from a monthly subscription.

The more indepth version:
I started playing MMO’s when City of Heroes was still a game for people to get excited for and upgrade their rigs to play. From that starting point I went on to play Guild Wars, World of Warcraft through all the expansions, Everquest, Runescape, and a few others. Rift is where I am currently finding myself spending a good portion of my gaming time. I was itching for another game that would fill that craving for a fun and grindy MMO and this is what I’ve landed on.

I have played Rift on and off over the past 3 years. Often installing it at the behest of my gaming group only for games to shift focus or real life responsibilities claiming my time. So with this urge to play an RPG coming around, and having burnt myself out of playing World of Warcraft’s newest expansion months ago, I decided to give Rift the attempt that it deserved.

My first impression of the game wasn’t great. I started to compare it to other games with a higher popularity and scrutinize over little details. For example, I don’t really like the characters animations in this game. They seem clunky, outdated, and unrealistic for a game that is trying to immerse you in it’s massive world. There are also a number of small hiccups and bugs throughout the game as a result of creating zones and not keeping up with them through patches. After leaving the starting area, I was more comfortable with the games purpose and mechanics. It felt like yet another “Wow Clone” and seemed simple enough to figure out. It wasn’t until about the third hour of gameplay that I really started to like Rift.

There always felt like something was going on and that there was adventure to be had. We would be killing X number of Y to collect Z when all of a sudden a rift would open up next to us. Not only did we fight to close it, we sort of felt obligated to. For those that haven’t played the game, Rifts open up around the zones and act as gates for creatures to come into our world from theirs. It acts as an Open Event that any number of players can take part in and all get currency that can be spent on items later in the game. There are also World Events that will start, where packs of enemies will move from place to place attacking and killing anything in sight. It makes for a progressive game that breaks up the monotonous questing and replaces it with options.

If questing and adventure aren’t your thing, there is plenty more to do to level up. At level 10 you unlock Instant Adventures, which are Raid-Style groups of players all scaled to the level of the zone you are brought to. Upon arrival the players are prompted with a world event that they take part in, often traveling all across the land to complete objectives. This was a feature that I especially liked about the game. After doing Dungeon Finder for years in World of Warcraft, I was very happy to see a different way to play the game that wasn’t just “Start here and fight to the finish line.” Some of the areas in Rift are gorgeous with very unique enemies, and getting to see how exciting the world gets at these higher levels only makes me want to continue playing the game.

To keep with the leaps and bounds of its peers, Rift also has a Dungeon Finder system that allows for grouping up with players. Something that really struck a chord with me was the depth that went into these simple dungeons. The first dungeon unlocks at level 15, and has hidden dialogue and story elements based on the quests that you acquire outside the dungeon. This is a nice touch above some of the simplicity of other games on the market. I’m very excited to see what the other dungeons have to offer in this game, as they are very reminiscent to classic MMORPG dungeon crawls.

To conclude, Rift is a very impressive game. I have played a number of Free-To-Play MMO’s over the years, and none have come close to offering what Rift does. The game doesn’t feel like it has a “pay to win” feature as some Free games do. The amount of stuff to do throughout the leveling process, the awesome community of players that stick through the game in its patches and renditions, the design of the zones and enemies, all keep me coming back with excitement to play.

So after reading the newest Dev diary, I decided to write a review for Hoi IV.
I really want to like this game, but I can't, because there is so much wrong in this game.
The First negative point is really immersion breaking.
The focus tree of several nations is historicaly not accurate
. In this review, I will only be talking about Japan.
Many important events for Japan are non existent, such as the
(feb. 1936), where the Kōdō-ha, one of two factions of the Japanese military, attempted a coup d'êtat. 1'500 soldiers attacked several buildings in Tokyo including police HQ's and the ministry of war and killed several high ranking politicians, including two former prime ministers.
The Goal of the Kōdō-ha, was to strenghten the emperor (without him agreeing) and make a change in governement, from a
to a militaristic facist type.
Yes, if you didn't know, Japan was in fact a democracy. At least in the beginning of WW2, with everything a democracy needed. Parlament, Prime ministers etc.
Another really important thing that is not represented in the game is that the Japanese Governement didn't have total control over it's own military in Korea, Manchukuo and the other conquered and puppeted nations.
In Hearts of Iron 4, Paradox has put Emperor Hirohito as leader of Japan and the party "Taisei Yokusankai" which has 100% popularity. The funny thing is the Taisei Yokusankai was not founded until 1940! Only after 1940 the japanese state transformed from a democracy to a single-party state.
The second big contra is the stupid AI.
I don't want to say much about it, after a couple hours learning the game and how to manage a good economy, you will beat the
AI pretty easily. After that you can still make them "harder", by giving them +% of production and stupid bonuses to Unit organization etc. I hate that, because the AI is still as stupid as before!
The AI still can't figure out how to properly do naval invasions, properly create division, they
(disabled by devs, since too hard to code), they can't guard their provinces and decrease unrest, oh yeah.. They are also not allowed to use licensing of equipment (too hard to code...?)
The only thing that makes the game
(not good enough) is by enabling mods.. which is really sad because Hoi IV should be a good game by itself. With all those updates that came out, which changed a lot of features, Hoi IV feels like it's still in the Alpha phase.
Did I mention that Paradox packs important features into the dlc's?

Hearts of Iron IV at its core is a good game, and due to that I will give it a recommended review. However, this is a good CASUAL game, and if you want something more serious, I would heavily reccomend starting out with Hearts Of Iron 3 instead. HOI4 improved in many aspects to HOI3 in terms of ease of use, but also lacked in some parts important to a strategy game.
Starting out with Pros:
The game is easy to get into, anyone can pick it up and be playing within an hour
Incredibly fun to play with friends over a discord call
Easy to use production systems
Equipment variant system not seen in the previous game
Mods can either make you more immersed or just provide silly and dumb fun
Fun zooming in and looking at the entirety of your front line with the models going about
Easy to go alternate history
Anyone can win any war, provided the conditions are correct
The graphics and general UI are improved
Easy to use multiplayer
Thanks to the workshop, easy to use mods
So, all of these mean that its a great casual game. However, then there's where it starts to lack in, which is quite a few areas.
Cons:
Horrendously bad, crazy, stupid AI. The AI in this game is TERRIBLE. Spamming divisions in peace time, terrible division design, production management, naval use, air usage, construction orders, basically everything.
The National Focus system is both good and bad, good for allowing the AI to easily go alternate history, bad because its basically also there to provide buffs and a clear path for the AI that would not even be remotely competent on its own.
National Focuses allow minor powers like Luxembourg to get jet aircraft before the major powers
The above point doesn't even matter because all you need to win is numbers in air battles, just spam out thousands of outdated fighters and bombers, it doesn't matter how many you lose if you have the air superiority bonus that just provides flat % buffs to your ground units.
The political power system is stupid, and so are research slots. HOI3 handled political power much, much better, allowing you to dedicate it into certain areas, like research, spying, or diplomacy.
Playing multiplayer games with people you don't know is a mixed bag
Lag starts to get horrendous if you have either a slow computer or internet
CORE GAME FEATURES MISSING AT LAUNCH, PROVIDED BY DLC.
---
All in all, even though I prefer HOI3 to this, HOI4 still has its appealing points, and is admittably much friendlier to use than HOI3.
TL;DR: hoi3 is better for realism and strategy, hoi4 is better for dumb fun with your friends or by yourself, and is easy to mod.

They Are Billions is very much a breath of fresh air in the RTS community, and especially in the zombie survival genre. I've been playing RTS games for over a decade, and this is easily both one of the most enjoyable and the most frustrating I've played.
They Are Billions makes you think, and think hard, about how you want to expand and grow your colony. You can't just spam units and expect to win. In the over 35 hours I've played so far, I've only won one time. There are others who are a lot better at this than I am, and win much more, but for the average player like me, it is a good challenge. More than once I've coem close to winning the current game, only to have my defenses fail at the last minute and the few surviving zombies annihilate my colony within a minute flat. It's both amazing and rage-inducing. But a great learning experience!
If you are into RTS games and need something new, look here. There is enough to keep you going for a long time. It requires both patience and aggression to win, and is a much resource management as it is warfare. I've not had it lag at all despite having thousands of zombies on screen at one time, and the art style works great with the steampunk angle of the game. I'm sure it will change some after I finish my review, but this is a very well polished beta and I sincerely hope it continues to grow and improve. There are some good guides to how to play the game, and plenty of YouTube videos to give you ideas and examples.

It’s … alright.
I wasn’t too sure what to say ‘bout the game but guess that’s the best way to describe it: it’s alright.
Nothing good and nothing bad.
…
Okay I can’t keep a straight face. I enjoy it. A lot. But there are of course a few things that really grind my gears. More on that later.
To give my fellow roguelike/lite lovers some info Rogue Continuum’s basically a mix between, you could say, Nuclear Throne and Hero Siege.
The whole game’s fast paced and plays like NT in a way but the, you could say, RPG elements of the game are basically just like HS.
Let me get into it.
So once you clear a mission or die in the process you receive some XP depending on how far you’ve come, how many enemies you’ve killed and so on.
Per level you gain with your character, of whom there are four, you gain one point to increase your stats and one point to level your abilities. Don’t know ‘bout you guys but that reminds me a lot of Hero Siege.
Let’s talk about one of the things I can’t seem to wrap my head around.
Prime example is Rufus. Now you see Rufus is a bad♥♥♥♥♥and deals a ton of damage by default BUT actually upgrading his Combust ability is just a waste of points in my opinion since the damage increases by one per level. By one. Really? Or Sam’s Rabid Fire. The duration also increases by one per level. It’s things like that that just make me wonder why we even have the option in the first place? On the other hand I fully understand it. If you play the game for let’s say 30 seconds then you really understand one thing: the game wants you dead.
It’s not easy. It MIGHT be easy once you’ve put some time and effort into your character but before that it’s teeth clenching time. For example there’s a lot of RNG in the game. Enemies spawn randomly in all kinds, items are always different and there’s always some kind of event that makes you hate life. On the very first mission for example there’s a space ship flying by like every 30 seconds or so (not too sure I’ve never cared to actually time it tbh) which drops bombs in a straight line damaging you and your enemies. More often than not it just damages you.
Anyway now that we got that tiny bit of salt out of the way let’s talk about the characters.
Now I’ve been told that the team has been working hard, for the better part of six months, on implementing multiplayer to the game. Currently only US servers are online and I wasn’t able to actually try it since there seems to be not that many people playing it as I’m writing this.
I’m mentioning this because the whole roster of characters you can choose just screams teamwork.
You’ve got the typical damage dealer called Smackdown Sam, a ranged damage dealer in the form of a sniper called Ownage Olga, a melee damage dealer/off-tank called Rampage Rufus and a full tank called Destructobot. See what I mean? Teamwork. Now before you freak out: yes all of them are able to solo the game. Some more, some less.
Sam starts out with a machine or shotgun and a skill which doubles his firing rate for five seconds.
Olga’s able to lay down a mine and uses various sniper rifles.
Rufus prefers chainsaws or swords with which he’s able to cut bullets and whatnot.
Destructobot uses missile pods and miniguns and he’s able to unleash a series of missiles.
So that’s your starter setup. While playing the game you’re able to find blueprints which unlock weapons which you then can find in crates.
You’re also able to upgrade your weapons with upgrade kits, which you also randomly find if you’re lucky, but as of yet you can’t seem to use them. For whatever reasons the game doesn’t register that you’ve actually found one.
What else?
Oh yeah. There’s a time travelling merchant selling you all kinds of things like damage reduction, health upgrades, cryobullets, combustion rounds and so on. In order to be able to buy something you need to kill stuff. In order to kill stuff you need stuff that kills stuff. And in order to get stuff that kills stuff you need to get stuff to get stuff that kills stuff. TL;DR: you need stuff.
In order to get all that stuff you just need to play the game. You see the game’s aimed towards the long term. I’ve been able to get to the third planet and I nearly killed the last boss on said planet but I got rekt so I figured it’s time to write a review for it.
There’s not too much to say about the game as of yet. It’s a fun game for every now and then.
You decide whether you spend mere minutes or hours with it. The choice is yours.
However. It isn’t easy. It’s not really hard either but it takes time to get used to it.
Considering that the game’s currently in early access you do get a solid game for the price.
So if you’re a fan of games like Nuclear Throne, Hero Siege or the roguelike genre in general it’s safe to say that you’ll find quite some enjoyment with Rogue Continuum.
Personally I really just hope that this isn’t it for the game if you know what I mean since it really seems to have a lot of potential.

You can't rate games on Steam without leaving a review so here's a once sentence review:
If you like arcade-style destructive point games this one is worth your time!

Note: This game was reviewed with a code provided by the developer this doesn't change my opinion on the game.
Dangerous Golf is the game developed by ex developers of Burnout. It provides golf and adds the crash mode from Burnout to provide a fun destruction game, but this falls flat within minutes of you starting playing it.
I was looking forward to playing this game and at first I enjoyed my time with it, but the more I played, the more my experience became a pain rather than enjoyment.
Dangerous Golf is a simple game. You are thrown into an environment and you are forced to destroy almost everything in sight and then sink in the put. This is pretty simple even later stages. After enough destruction you are given a smashbreaker bar which lights your golf ball on fire and you explode everything you touch. It brings in more strategy in this game, but however this isn't wanted and you just want to cause as much destruction as possible.
The events stay regularly the same and there's an event at the end of each tour which is there to test your skills, but it's probably the easiest event out of all of them and the most relaxing as well.
Graphically the game looks stunning. The UNREAL 4 engine lighting and destruction look glorious and it's just amazing. One of my favorite features is the game letting you do a flyby of the level and then after you are finished with the level you have a flyby of the level after you destroyed the hell out of it.
The game is also quite buggy. The golf ball glitches through walls, smashbreaker balls get stuck in walls and furniture models clipping with each other when you destroy them. The golf ball going through walls happened frequently on my playthrough and I really hope this issue is fixed.
The game is also too long for it's own good. There are around 100 courses to go through and all of them are the same, by the time you unlock World Tour 4 you have pretty much seen everything. It get's insanely boring by the end of it. I had to take long breaks after playing for a while cause I was incredibly bored while playing it.
The game took me 5 hours to finish everything. There is also a Co Op mode and you can try acing every level, but it's insanely hard, so I doubt it's worth trying to achieve that.
The game also has abysmal keyboard and mouse controls so only play if you have a controller cause otherwise there's no point.
Overall Dangerous Golf is a rough game, for the price you can get your moneys worth, if you absolutely loved Burnouts Crash Mode, but Burnout had a full game attached to it, but in my opinion this game is kind of boring and only worth getting on sale, but I still suggest skipping it.
Pros:
+ Amazing Visuals

Cons:
- Too Boring
- Glitches
- Keyboard Controls are horrible
4/10

Fast Forward to the 2015 Summer Sale.
I bought 3 copies of Hatoful Boyfriend - again, on a huge sale. I'm the cheap friend - and gave two of the copies to friends, and saved one for myself to play for some small laughs. Get an ending or two, waste some time. But as I got more endings, I learned more and more about the world I was thrown into, and just how intriguing it was. And I learned more and more about the characters I'm around, and how everything fits together more than one would find in a simple dating simulator - human or otherwise.
Three and a half hours later:
I have gone through eight different endings. I have nearly cried twice, and completely ragequit once. I have been piecing the world together and it is an outstanding place. I have come to understand just why it is worth its full pricetag, and feel dirty having only paid a cut price for this.
In short, Hatoful Boyfriend is a top contender to being one of my favorite games ever. It deserves the chance to being yours too.
