Despite all the bad reviews, I really enjoyed The Bureau: XCOM Declassified. It's not a perfect game and many things could have been done different, but I had a lot of fun beating the game and it's nice to go back again to the Xcom universe, even if the game has, gameplay-wise, nothing to do with the former games of the franchise.
Giving commands was neat, the controls were okay, the voice acting was excellent, the story was okaysh at first, and awesome at the end and during my almost 20 hour playthrough I encountered just one bug, which was easily fixed by reloading the last checkpoint. I played it on the hardest difficulty, so I am not sure this always applies, but the fights were sometimes just too long. Even on the hardest difficulty, it was not as hard as I imagined it would be, but you do have to plan your men movements and always stay behind cover. The variety of enemies is nice and the abilities in the field were a lot of fun to use and combine. Combat was similar to the one in Mass Effect, but there was almost no interaction with anyone in the base and when there was, it was pretty boring. I liked the layout of the maps, though, and how they were all very detailed and were usually used to convey little stories, which can be ignored completely if you want to rush to the end though. Yes, the maps are certainly linear, but I think they were supposed to be that way, just as in most games.
So, although the game may not be perfect, I had a lot of fun playing it and defending Earth once again against the aliens. The story got awesome towards the end and it actually leaves you thinking about it. So yeah, I definitely recommend The Bureau: Xcom Declassified... as long as you understand this has little to do with Xcom: Enemy Unknown. They may share the Xcom part, but whereas EU is completely innovative and one of my favorite games for a reason, The Bureau is just an average shooter that will grant you about 15 hours of shooting and fun. Both great games, but completely different genres. I say go for it!

I am updating my review from negative to positive.  Here's why:
At first I hated this game, but my son wanted me to play with him, and after a few days, I have actually found the hard work involved to be very rewarding.  There are annoyances, such as the deaths from dehydration, the limited battery life of your flashlight.  The rarity of Lithium, and the absurd quantities of ore needed to build the smallest things.  But the game is still developing, and after learning the landscape and its resources I can now easily see that I was approaching the game all wrong.  But most of all... the vehicles are amazing!  Totally worth the wait!
I've taken the time to learn the game, and even started helping update the Wiki site.
First, if you want to buy this game, WAIT.   Don't pay full price for it yet.  Wait until the full release.
Secondly, play the game with a friend.  Don't try and grind the required resources alone.  With two or more players, the game will be much more fun.
The first few literal days of this game are brutally difficult if you don't know what you're doing.
Read the Osiris New Dawn Wiki before you just dive in.  There are subtle details you'll miss because the game isn't finished, and doesn't tell you exactly what to do to survive.  There's no tutorial yet.
HOWEVER, despite my initial irritation with this game I can now say that I have had a LOT of fun with it.
Once you get established, build a base, and a hovercraft, you'll start to feel rewarded for all your hard work and suffering.  The game does a terrible job at easing you into itself, but if you stick with it the payoff feels fun.
>Aliens that once harassed you and felt menacing now suddenly feel like ants as you squash them with your Ground Assault Vehicle.
>Resources that were once a day and half away are now only seconds away as you speed your hover craft across the terrain.
>Space Ships are now just within your grasp, and soon you'll be flying among the stars!
The game is slow paced, but with patience and dealing with the obnoxious learning curve has left me with a great gaming experience in the end.
Alas, this game is in Alpha/Early Access, and so I have encountered a couple of bugs/glitches.
One bug even left me stranded on a new planet without access to my space ship.  So I've literally found myself starting from scratch and slowly dying as I try to rebuild another space ship on a new world.
Nonetheless, we're having fun with it.

Came back after many years, found a world where everything was teleporting and rubber-banding about.  I'd shoot at enemies and they'd vanish, so I'd try to walk away, only to find a few seconds later I would be zapped over to some new location and locked in melee with that foe - who was still standing fifty feet away in another direction, but we were in melee anyway.
Also I discovered that I could now walk through walls.  This seemed awesome at first until I tried to go back into town but realized that I couldn't, because instead of climbing stairs I just kept walking through them instead.
At no point during this experiment did I ever see another actual human player.
As for the parts that did still work... well, it was never impressive to begin with.  The entire MMO industry has degraded itself into little more than a machine to produce WoW clones, and this game is no exception.  The graphics may change and maybe, just maybe, some games will add a whole
faction (this one does not), but in the end it's all the same tropes, the same combat, the same classes, the same mounts, the same grind and the same empty, meaningless themepark ride for a world full of "chosen ones" that only exists to be a barrier between the new player and the max level guild/clan raiding gang - the "whales" of the industry who can always be counted on to trade in their college fund for a one point PvP advantage that only lasts until the next DLC/expansion pack comes out.
In other words, if you've played any three other fantasy MMOs in your lifetime then you've already played RIFT, or at least you may as well have.  You've already seen everything that you'd see in this game.  If you still want to put yourself through this year's re-skinning of that same game then have fun with that, but to me it doesn't matter what kind of sauce you put on tofu - it's still just tofu.
Now you may not agree with this but again, not one other human player this time around and honestly, I never saw more than half a dozen outside of the towns even when the game was brand new.  So don't just take my word on it - look around.  Forget the zombie survival games,
is your real "Last Man on Earth" experience right here.

they're trying to get everyone to buy a $40DLC.  That last cash influx will make for nice golden little parachute for the company executives  who are probably laughing all the way to their banks in Switzerland before pulling the life support on this vegetable and heading off to the magical realm of comfy retirement.

I purchased this game on sale for 50 cents, and that's about what it's worth. There are four maps each with roughly the same play style, you're either the gunner or a runner. The gunner stops the other players from reaching the finish line, while the runners attempt to reach the finish line. That's about it. The game generally lacks substance, but makes up for it with the price tag. I had a good time playing this game and would recommend it to anyone looking to kill time with a group of friends. You'll more than likely, with the right people, get a couple good hours of gameplay out of it. I would however, recommend waiting for the game to go on sale, seeing that I don't personally feel it to be worth $2.99. When asked if I would recommend this game, I find it hard to give a concrete answer. For 50 cents, I would certainly recommend it. For $2.99, possibly, but more than likely not.
TLDR; All in all a good and enjoyable time killer but lacks substance, you'll likely get an hour or two out of it. Wait for a sale.

The gameplay can be fun but is mostly awful for the gunner. One player is the gunner while three players are runners. There are four maps in total, and each one has a different gun system. "Clouds" is the best map because it is the only map in which the gunner has a reasonable chance of victory. "Classic" is less fair to the gunner but provided my group great laughs as dodgeballs and volleyballs were launched at us. "Canyon" and "Corners" were awful to play on for the gunner.
The art is mediocre at best. The art design clashes with realistic textures on some environments and a cartoony look for the runners. The game is full of amateur art, but character designs like &quot♥♥♥♥♥♥Gentlemen" are unique. The character models are mostly lifeless, as the models barely move anything except their legs when running. The environments are plain but contrast well with the weapons.
The background music and sound design were not notable.
My group ran into a few bugs in our playtime. Choosing roles did not work for us. If only one person chose gunner and everyone else was a runner, the game would still select someone else as the gunner. Once, a runner spawned outside of bounds and was unable to play that round. Sound effects often did not play.
I would improve the game by removing the ammo limits for the guns, except in the case of explosives. "Clouds" was the most fun to play on because it was a challenge for the runners as the gunner had ample ammunition to attack with. I would also unify the art to a cartoony style.

I can't actually run Evolve:Stage 2, so instead, here is an excellent pizza recipe.
Ingredients:
For the base
300g strong bread flour
1 tsp instant yeast
(from a sachet or a tub)
1 tsp salt
1 tbsp olive oil
, plus extra for drizzling
For the tomato sauce
100ml passata
handful fresh basil
or 1 tsp dried
1 garlic clove, crushed
For the topping
125g ball mozzarella, sliced
handful grated or shaved Parmesan
(or vegetarian alternative)
handful cherry tomatoes, halved
To finish
handful basil
leaves (optional)
Method:
Make the base: Put the flour into a large bowl, then stir in the yeast and salt. Make a well, pour in 200ml warm water and the olive oil and bring together with a wooden spoon until you have a soft, fairly wet dough. Turn onto a lightly floured surface and knead for 5 mins until smooth. Cover with a tea towel and set aside. You can leave the dough to rise if you like, but it’s not essential for a thin crust.
Make the sauce: Mix the passata, basil and crushed garlic together, then season to taste. Leave to stand at room temperature while you get on with shaping the base.
Roll out the dough: If you’ve let the dough rise, give it a quick knead, then split into two balls. On a floured surface, roll out the dough into large rounds, about 25cm across, using a rolling pin. The dough needs to be very thin as it will rise in the oven. Lift the rounds onto two floured baking sheets.
Top and bake: Heat oven to 240C/fan 220C /gas 8. Put another baking sheet or an upturned baking tray in the oven on the top shelf. Smooth sauce over bases with the back of a spoon. Scatter with cheese and tomatoes, drizzle with olive oil and season. Put one pizza, still on its baking sheet, on top of the preheated sheet or tray. Bake for 8-10 mins until crisp. Serve with a little more olive oil, and basil leaves if using. Repeat step for remaining pizza.
Enjoy your pizza!

Evolve is one of those games that almost never gets boring, his wide variety of characters, playstiles, gamemodes and perks make it have a huge replayability potential., plus, it gets updated frequently, often adding even more characters or maps, and even recently, a new gamemode.
As stated, the characters are very different from one another, and they all have different weapons, which makes for intersting combinations when it comes to fighting the monster. I also really like the fact that some of the characters swear from time to time, not that it is vital, but it is good to see swears haven't been censored for once, a small plus, i'd say. Also adding that some of the characters and dialogs are down right hilarious too.
Speaking of monsters, those too are different from one another, some are ground ones like goliath, behemoth, or even gorgon, while some others are more aerial, like kraken or elder kraken. Those aerials one can be a problem when it comes to, let's say, a Lennox, or a Hyde, that both have really short ranges, and either need to fly up to the monster, or rely on their less powerful, but still viable and reliable secondaries.
The new gamemode, with the gorgon queen is the best thing i have played in a long, long time, the dark atmosphere and creepy voice narrator just add to the feeling of insecurity, becaue unlike in normal hunt, the map is shrouded in the night, and trappers can't use their planet scanner, often making for situations when the Gorgon queen, or even little Gorgons, will leap out of the shadow and try to slay you, what keeps you on the edge of your seat. The only problem i see with this new gamemode would be the difficulty and the way of playing needed, lemme explain: first, the Gorgon queen herself is incredibly strong, she has a huge HP pool, has powerful attacks, but all in all, ressembles to just a big Gorgon, thing is, it is a bot, what is understandable, since no human could play that way, that AI makes it an easy target, sometime, she will incapacitate a teammate, and target another one, you can litterally walk up to the guy, start reanimating him, even if the gorgon sees you and is one meter away, she won't attak you, but keep focus. And, as said previously, this plays a tiny bit differently than regular gamemodes, in this one, it's all about DPS and survivability, unlike in regular, when the "running after the boss for 5 minutes" is added, that makes for situations when you will almost always big DPS hunters, not that it is a ad thing, but then weaker ones get overshadowed, like, you will mostly always have a Rogue Val, a Palladin Parnell or even a Caira, rather than a character than is usually more versatile, like Emet or Lazarus.
It is also important to say, that there are obviously better hunters or monsters, there is a really good guide that explains this very well, but keep in mind, that a good player can make a weak character good, and a bad player can make a strong character weak, adding this to the character level up, which gives you an idea if you have a chance, like, if you see a level 40 elder kraken, and you are the only level 20+ in your team, you know it won't last long.
If i had to find another problem, i'd say new characters are either always OP or UP, like Quantum Caira is nowhere as good as the regular Caira, whilst Electro Griffin is, in my opinion, much more powerful and easy to play than the regular. But that is just nitpicking.
(yes, i'll just keep going)
Another thing, is the team composition, as you probably know, there are 4 members in one team, each having a different role, and i swear, this is the first time i can play medic and have fun, without being a punching bag for the enemy, most medics have a really good DPS, like Lazarus or Palladin Parnell, and can defend themselves, some medics even got a better dps than some other hunters, like Jack, who has a really low one.
The addition of weapon, hunter and monsters skins, adds to the game in a good way, sure, ultimately most people will use the elite skins, but on lower levels, most hunters and monsters have alternative ones that allows you to customize your character, to a small extend.
The lore of the game is also really interesting, most of it is explained ingame before the beginning of the mission, while in the dropship, different characters will interact with each others, giving informations about the game's lore, the character's backstories, and that kinda stuff, it's a creative way of giving out informations, unlike having a narrator, or having you read walls of text, like the one you are reading right now. But these dialogs aren't only to expose the story, it is also to keep you entertained during the dropship "scene" that plays at the beginning of each round, giving the monster some time to run away.
My last argument for this game would be the attention to detail, and the graphism, who are, in my opinion, really well executed here. Firstly, the game is beautiful, it has awesome graphics, all characters and monsters have a great design, as well as weapons. Secondly, the attention to detail is huge, for example, in most games, when you shoot an animal, no matter when you hit, the thing will either run away, die, or attack, here, when attacking regular wildlife, you can either do more damage, what is kinda generic, but teaches you to aim, or if you get it low enough on hp or shoot it's leg, it will start crawling and screaming, that only adds to the realism of the game itself.
So, to conclude, i would say Evolve is a great game, and bound to get better over time, with his active fanbase, and it's developpers bringing new content regularly, i have many hopes for this game.

I share a similar story with many other reviewers here. I bought this game for the laughs. I mean, a pigeon dating sim? I assumed I'd have fun with it for a couple of hours and then be done. I was not expecting what happened next.
I must admit that there are negatives, and I will point them out before I praise the game. To start off, I'm not sure if this can be considered a negative (I think it's a positive), but a few of the story lines seem to be created merely for amusement and humour. They make no sense, and are there as a joke. However, If you are looking for something that is 100% serious, you're in the wrong place, and I have absolutely no clue why you would be here in the first place. Anyway, the interface and skill point system is simple, but they do the job. There are a few spelling and grammar errors scattered throughout, which may be distracting, but they are far and few between. As well, the starting routes are short and perhaps shallow. I recommend you try to complete all of the endings in order to see the "Bad Boys Love" bonus ending and the epilogue.
Despite all of that, this game sets you on an emotional roller coaster if you put in the time to explore the different routes, and carry through with the finale. With various endings, each path provides a unique narrative. If the final ending is achieved, all of the stories tie together quite well, leaving you with an unexpectedly profound story, a group of memorable characters, and a collection of bird puns.
I came for the laughs. What I got was comedy, romance, horror, mystery, and tears.
I didn't ask for this.
But I'm glad it happened.

The Bureau: XCOM Declassified is the imagination of a classic series of turn based strategy games as a first person shooter.  The game begins in Pima, New Mexico where strange happenings are afoot and suddenly a coordinated alien strike disrupts global communications, supply lines, etc.  The Bureau is an over-the-shoulder shooter with a “time-slow” button that allows the player to give commands to their squad.  Those who have played the Mass Effect games … the combat is exactly like Mass Effect.
The Good:  The fights in this game a pretty fun.  Good battlefield layout made for lots of fun fights as you slip from cover to cover. Further, the ability to move your squaddies and deploy skills and hardware gave a neat strategic over lay that made the game more than just a “shoot-em-in-the-head-over-and-over” fest (in lower difficulties).
The Bad: Sadly, everything else is ranging from not good to terrible.  The entire game is one long hall way; there’s never two ways to a fight, a way around a fight, etc.  The story … well dang, I am honor bound to never spoil anything no matter how good or how bad I think the writing may be.  That said I’ll be interested to talk to someone else who’s played this to see if the whole last 10% of the game was actually as bad as it seemed of it is super wonderful and I’m just a dope and didn’t get it … IDK, not worth playing again to find out.  The voice acting is mediocre at best and the tech-tree (or extreme lack thereof) is downright offensive to anyone who’s played the older X-Com games (there is no tech tree, you find a weapon just sitting there and pick it up … yours now).  The game is also SO comically straight forward that you almost have to avoid the “secrets” since they are mostly shiny things at the end of short hallways, like … you can nearly see them from the main rout!  Just in case you actually did miss anything the stuff in these “secret” passages you can take comfort in that it is either ammo you didn’t need or a gear schematic that they game will give you later.  This game also commits the cardinal sin of game difficulty: enemies get more HP and do more damage / run a head-shot script per level of difficulty which turns the game into a “shoot-em-in-the-head-over-and-over” fest.
The Funny: The game was also not bug free which, when games are bad, can be nice since it serves as comic relief.  I fell through the floor of places I was walking toward twice and once the camera locked onto my face and didn’t move after dialog.  The combat raged on and I proceeded to just sit there, adoring the main characters steely grimace while getting gunned down for being out of cover.  OH!  Whether or not you play the game though, be sure to look up the commercials!  The marketing for this game was more fun than the entire game!  Seriously, the stuff they did on Twitter and small webisodes and such were SUPERB!  The marketing people for this deserve to be on much better projects that’s for sure!  I’d hire then in a snap!
The Summary:  I give this game 5 out of 10.  It’s not quite as bad as when they made Shadowrun into FPS but this is pretty bad.  Think of a game like Chess.  We know it as a game where strategy and a careful, mistake free execution are keys to success.  Then take the strategy out and let all the chess pieces run anywhere they want and shoot!  That’s what you get when you turn a game like X-Com into an FPS.  If you want to sit down and shoot at aliens for a few hours while you watch TV and the game is on Steam-sale for 5 bucks or less you won’t kick yourself for picking up a copy, I’ll give it that.  With all the good titles out there though I can’t imagine anyone so hard up for something to do that this would be a good buy.  The fights are fun if ya like a quick shoot-em-up but that’s all I can say.  Thank God Sid Meyers got the rights to this game as well and made a FANTASTIC turn based strategy X-Com; that is everything X-Com should have been!  GET THAT ONE INSTEAD!

This game is amazingly fun and difficult. Let me give an example of how did it go for first few games.
There are two difficulty settings (number of zombies, and how much time you have to prepare for final attack). Each has like five settings. These two difficulties combined give a single score expressed in percent. Starts from 7% and ends close to 400%. I assume the intent is that 100% is you actual goal, and above 100% is for insane skills and some luck (maps are randomized).
The game has pause function, so, how difficult can it be? I thought. Just pause, give all orders, read everything you want, etc. But just in case I started my first game on the easiest (lowest out of 5 for each settings) with the difficulty score of 7%. Constantly pausing. Reading everything. ... and... loosing. A game with pause. On lowest settings. Wow! But it was very fun. So, I started the second game, also at lowest settings, and it was much easier, since I knew what to expect. By the end of the game it was nearly boring. And I won, indeed easily.
So, my third game was at higher settings in both difficulties. Coincidently, you need to win with more than 20% difficulty to get the second map. And I lost that game near the end. Tried several times more, and I was losing quite earlier, because I was greedy and was trying to get large territory to begin with and missing just one zombie. When zombie gets through your defenses, it infects house, spraying more zombies, and this avalanche killed me like 3 times. Finally I understood my problem and won this settings as well. Now, I feel I can do better and playing a new map with higher difficulties.
As you can see, there is a constant progress of learning, of trying different things. If you stuck, watch some youtube videos, you will see some tricks there.
Overall, this is very challenging and fantastic game that gives you feeling of accomplishment when you win even with the easiest settings. And you have seen the graphics - they are simply amazing.
